newsitem.title: USA: Ansan sees charge over escrowed shares.
newsitem.headline: Ansan sees charge over escrowed shares.

text.p: Ansan Pharmaceuticals Inc said Monday it expects to report a substantial one-time charge if shares curently under escrow in connection with its 1995 initial public offering are released.
Ansan, a San Francisco-based pharmaceutical company in development stage, made the disclosure in a quarterly financial report to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
It said certain stockholders placed 365,983 common shares into escrow pending the company's reaching certain revenue or share price targets.
In addition, it said current holders of certain options exercisable at less than the IPO price of $5.00, placed options to buy 34,017 shares similarly under escrow.

Ansan said that, for accounting purposes, it is the SEC's position that when the escrowed shares are released to its directors, officers, employees or consultants, the company should treat it as compensation expense.
Ansan noted that the one-time charge "would substantially increase the companys's loss or reduce or eliminate earnings, if any" when the charge is taken.
It said that the compensation expense to be recognized will not affect total stockholders' equity.
